chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: The Streets of Paris, Kay Starr, Helen Humes and Erroll Garner upstairs
summary: Six months at the Streets of Paris with singers, with Garner playing nearby at the Susie Q.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: said, "Well, I've got another club down the street called The Streets of Paris; I'll put you there. But we've got a conflict here." I said, "Well, okay. All right, as long as I've got a job." The work was on. I didn't mind.

So we were in the Streets of Paris, and we stayed there for about I guess six months, a little better than six months. They had Kay Starr in there with me, too, and this blues singer that used to be with Basie... Helen Humes. She was in there with me, too. So we had a good thing... And Erroll Garner was right upstairs, in the Susie Q.
Was that right up from Streets of Paris?
Yeah. Right up about two doors. He was right there. They were right on the corner.
You say upstairs. Do you mean the Streets of Paris was a below-level club...

Yeah. But it was downstairs. Which was nice. And I could go in and hear Garner whenever I wanted to. It was very nice. It was much better than the Jade Room, because in the Jade Room the only thing I could hear was them old-time tunes, and God knows, I was sick of hearing them. Because I done played "Sweet Georgia Brown" so much and all the traditional tunes that they played... I come up playing that stuff. So I mean, like, I was glad to get away from that.
And Garner played... You know, he played a different style of music that I liked. It wasn't a Modernist thing, it never was, but he played good!
